why_it_supports_the_claim: ELECTROPERU (Peruvian state-owned hydroelectric generation company, operator of the Mantaro hydro complex) is the subject/author of its own formal 2021 software-evaluation report (Informe Técnico Previo de Evaluación de Software N°006-2021-GT) assessing four long/medium/short-term operation-optimization software alternatives to independently verify/replicate the national system operator COES's dispatch decisions and support ELECTROPERU's own commercial bidding strategy. PLEXOS (Alternativa 4) scored highest on both technical (79 vs 57) and benefit/cost (1.124 vs 0.712) criteria against the incumbent SDDP+NCP combination, and Annex 2 contains a formal PLEXOS licensing quotation and PLEXOS training proposal addressed to ELECTROPERU staff. A later ELECTROPERU accountability report (2022) lists 'Desarrollo de destrezas en el manejo de herramientas de optimización de la operación (Plexos)' as an improvement action, corroborating that the organization proceeded from evaluation toward operational skill-building with PLEXOS one year after the evaluation. Extra scrutiny applied (second-pass per 3-day-budget rule, Q5/Q8): the 2022 sentence alone is forward-looking/aspirational ('desarrollo de destrezas' = developing skills, not 'we use'), so evidence_classification is based on the combination of the 2021 evaluation (PLEXOS selected as best-scoring alternative, formal quotation obtained) plus the 2022 corroborating skill-development reference, not on either document alone -- see unresolved_questions.md for this chain-of-evidence judgment call. Classified current given the most recent corroborating document is from 2022/2023.

why_it_supports_the_claim: Prayas (Energy Group), a Pune-based Indian non-profit policy research organization (registered SIRO under India's Dept of Scientific and Industrial Research), directly built and ran its own PLEXOS model of the Maharashtra power system in 2019, prior to migrating to the open-source GridPath platform for a 2021 follow-up study. The 2021 report's own methodology section states: 'The model is set up in a way similar to that in an earlier study by the authors using the commercial power system modelling platform, PLEXOS (PEG, 2019) (Dukkipati, Dixit, Gambhir, & Chitnis, 2019)...The earlier PLEXOS model is modified with the same inputs as the GridPath model, and the results from both these models are compared. The versions of these platforms used for this analysis are version 0.8.2 of GridPath and version 7.500R04 of PLEXOS' [10]. Independently corroborated by Prayas's own December 2019 webinar description (same Dukkipati/Gambhir/Dixit authorship): 'This exercise involved granular (15 min block) system simulation using the PLEXOS platform and shows that 50% of electricity demand can be met by RE sources without any adverse economic or reliability implications' [11]. Historical: the original PLEXOS study dates to 2019; Prayas's own 2021 report explicitly states they subsequently moved to the open-source GridPath platform citing commercial-tool cost and black-box transparency concerns for Indian stakeholders ('Commercial tools, though popular and feature-rich, are unaffordable to a wide range of stakeholders in India...the black box nature of these closed-source tools makes them unsuitable for public consultation processes'), so no evidence of continuing PLEXOS use was found -- flagged historical rather than current. why_it_supports_the_claim: MENA/Gulf new hit found via a systematic IRENA/CIF/GCF/USAID/GIZ sweep (searching IRENA Gulf-states renewable-integration studies led to this primary source). EWEC (the single buyer and seller of water and electricity in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi) states in its own official 2021-2027 Statement of Future Capacity Requirements: 'In preparing this Statement, all modelling work has been carried out by the EWEC planning team with drafting support from NERA Economic Consulting.' The document explicitly names 'The PLEXOS power and water system production cost model, to evaluate optimal capacity expansion projects' as one of two analytical models used, and repeatedly describes PLEXOS results in first person ('Our PLEXOS modelling suggests...', 'Since the 2019 Statement, we have made a number of improvements to the PLEXOS modelling infrastructure'). NERA Economic Consulting provided only drafting support (not modeling) per EWEC's own acknowledgment, so NERA is not recorded as consultant_modeler for this engagement -- EWEC's own planning team is the party that built and ran the PLEXOS model, warranting direct_user. This upgrades MENA/UAE coverage beyond the prior academic-only evidence (Heriot-Watt Dubai research_user, ORG-AFME-0016): EWEC is a genuine government-adjacent utility (single buyer/seller for Abu Dhabi, reporting to the Department of Energy) running its own PLEXOS model for official annual capacity planning, not a third-party research study. source_title: Hawai’I Asia pacific Regional Energy System Assessment (APRESA)  ASEAN Interconnection Masterplan Study (AIMS) III Support
exact_snippet_or_quote: HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE), an intergovernmental organization within the ASEAN structure representing the AMS interests in the energy sector, on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study.
why_it_supports_the_claim: DEDICATED FOLLOW-UP per unresolved_questions.md batch63_regional_subject flag: investigated ACE itself (Jakarta-based ASEAN intergovernmental secretariat), not the ASEAN member states, as a direct_user/commissioner candidate for the AIMS III regional PLEXOS study. ACE's own AIMS III Phase 1&2 Report states 'The Head of the ASEAN Power Utilities/Authorities (HAPUA) Council appointed the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) as the Implementing Agency (IA)' and 'The AIMS III Report was jointly developed by ACE and the national experts from the ASEAN Member States as part of the AIMS III Working Group, with GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant' [2]. 'The capacity expansion planning task was made with PLEXOS using Energy Exemplar as the simulation tool' [2] -- confirming PLEXOS as the actual tool used to build the AIMS III capacity-expansion model. ACE's own news page independently corroborates that ACE selected and directed GE Energy Consulting as the PLEXOS-running consultant: 'ACE with its selected consultant to lead the works of AIMS III, GE Consortium, wisely welcomed the inputs and feedbacks from all TRG members' [3]. HNEI/GridSTART's own project page confirms ACE itself received hands-on PLEXOS training, but frames it as management-oversight capacity rather than production modeling: 'HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE)...on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study' [1]. ROLE JUDGMENT (8-question evaluator checklist applied): (1) Is PLEXOS named? Yes, explicitly and repeatedly in ACE's own report. (2) Is the org named as doing something specific with it? why_it_supports_the_claim: The Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis's own Energy Unit (within the Ministry of Public Infrastructure, Energy & Utilities, Domestic Transport) directly names PLEXOS as an operational modeling tool used by its own staff, not merely a consultant's tool. A 2024 government vacancy notice for 'Senior Engineer -- Energy Unit' lists among the role's actual Duties and Responsibilities: 'Development of national power systems models using PLEXOS;' alongside 'Integrated Resource and Resiliency Planning (IRRP)' and 'Liaison with SKELEC, CARICOM Secretariat, the Caribbean Centre for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency (CCREEE) and other regional partners.' The required Knowledge & Skills section repeats: 'PLEXOS or the equivalent, LEAP or the equivalent, Integrated Resource Planning and/or Integrated Resource and Resilience Planning (IRRP).' A companion 2023 vacancy notice for 'Director of the Energy Unit' (ledger id 4) corroborates at the leadership level: 'Experience with production cost modelling using software such as PLEXOS, PROMOD, UPLAN or the equivalent within the context of economic analysis for electric utility integrated resource planning (IRP).' Unlike a generic consultancy job posting listing PLEXOS alongside competing tools as candidate background (the catalogue's standard false-positive risk, per the plexos-org-catalogue-research skill), this is a GOVERNMENT AGENCY's own stated job duties for operating PLEXOS as part of its own national IRRP -- the agency itself, not a hired consultant, is the entity described as running the software. Classified direct_user. Current: live/recent vacancy notices (2023, 2024) describing an ongoing, standing government function, not a one-off historical engagement.

use_case: ORNL researchers used PyPSA (version 0.24.0) as the power network solver, coupled with EPANET for water, to simulate network rebalancing following transmission line outages in a cascading-failure study of synthetic power and water networks for the City of Phoenix.
summary: Used PyPSA in research to simulate network rebalancing after transmission line outages in a cascading-failure study of the City of Phoenix.
source_title: Cascading Failure Propagation and Perfect Storms in Interdependent Infrastructures
exact_snippet_or_quote: Using the City of Phoenix as a case study, synthetic power and water networks are constructed and coupled, and disturbances are simulated to capture cascading failure behaviors within and across power and water distribution systems. Network solvers [PyPSA (version 0.24.0) for power and EPANET (version 2.2) for water] are used to capture network rebalancing. Failures are simulated starting with transmission line outages and 120,000 simulations used to capture stochasticity in the rebalancing of power and water systems.
why_it_supports_the_claim: ORNL's own publication page states that PyPSA version 0.24.0 was used as the power network solver in their cascading-failure simulation work.
notes: First-party evidence from ORNL's publication page (snippet verbatim). Study uses a synthetic Phoenix power/water network as case study, so usage is for research simulation rather than an operational planning product. ORNL also appears in this catalogue's PLEXOS rows; this is a separate PyPSA finding.
